study: studies/identifiability/qmatrix-positivity (per-edge Q-matrix positivity, Gu & Xu 2024 Prop. 1, against the positivity atlas)
note: IS F1'S LIMIT THE ITEM DESIGN OR THE LEARNER ORDER? For every candidate edge A->B the atlas scores, does the corpus's Q-matrix hold an item measuring B without A? Pre-registered (thresholds and verdict strings committed before real data); synthetic floor passed (counter exact against brute force on 39,800 planted pairs; dense replica equal to the atlas's own functions on every pair); the atlas reproduced EXACTLY per edge on all three corpora (XES3G5M 736/69/19,195, Eedi 4,935/138/14,927, ASSISTments 87/0/39,913 supported/contradicted/unknown). PRIMARY VERDICT LEARNER-ORDER-LIMITED on all three: share of undecided edges unidentified by design f = 0.010% [0, 0.038%] XES3G5M (2 of 19,195), 0.020% [0, 0.059%] Eedi (3 of 14,927), 0% ASSISTments (Q is a partition, so vacuous); census 151 of 747,360 and 18 of 94,556 ordered pairs. Design-unidentified edges are all undecided (DESIGN NESTED IN LEARNER LIMIT) but are a vanishing part of the undecided set: the two limits fall on different edges, and no supported edge is design-unidentified. STRICT READING (no item measuring B alone): f = 16.7% [14.3%, 19.1%] XES3G5M and 8.2% [4.8%, 12.0%] Eedi, MIXED; 40 of XES3G5M's 736 supported edges point into such dependants. The within-dependant derangement null was degenerate, so the direction test is uninformative. Exploratory: co-tagged edges are decided far more often (Eedi 64% vs 25.4%). Moves nothing.
